meta.documentTitle: Mahabharat Episode 6: The Birth of Devavrata

header.title: Mahabharat Episode 6: The Birth of Devavrata
header.description: The tragic fate of Shantanu and Ganga's first seven children, the cosmic backstory of Sage Vasishta's curse on the Vasus, and the rise of Devavrata.

intro.title: The Silent Heartbreak of a King
leads: Ganga gave birth to a fine son, but as soon as the child was born, she carried him straight to the river and drowned him.
King Shantanu was devastated, yet he remained silent—knowing that if he dared to question her actions, she would leave him forever.
Child after child was born, and without a single word of explanation, Ganga drowned seven newborn sons in succession, pushing Shantanu to the brink of insanity.

storyElements.html: When the eighth infant was born, Shantanu could no longer contain his agony and followed Ganga helplessly to the riverbank.
Just as she was about to submerge the child into the water, Shantanu grabbed the infant from her hands.

bubble.text: Enough! Why are you doing such inhuman things?
You have broken our sacred condition, and now it is time for me to go. But I owe you an explanation, so let me tell you why this had to happen.

storyElements.text: Sage Vasishta and the Eight Vasus

storyElements.html: Long ago, Sage Vasishta lived in his ashram with a divine, wish-fulfilling cow named Nandini.
Eight Vasus (celestial beings) were traveling through the region in self-driven flying crafts that glided smoothly like liquid mercury and burned with fireless light.
While visiting Vasishta's ashram, the wife of a Vasu named Prabhasa saw Nandini and demanded to have her.
When the other Vasus hesitated, Prabhasa's wife accused them of cowardice. Driven by pride, Prabhasa and his companions stole the sage's divine cow.
Discovering the theft, Sage Vasishta cursed all eight Vasus for violating hospitality.

bubble.text: May you be born as mortal human beings with all their physical limitations! Your wings shall be clipped, and you must endure life and death upon Earth.

storyElements.html: Terrified, the Vasus begged Ganga to take them into her womb and liberate them from Earth as quickly as possible.

bubble.text: I was only fulfilling their request to end their earthly curse quickly. The first seven are now liberated, but this eighth child is Prabhasa—the main instigator—who was destined for a longer life on Earth.

storyElements.html: Ganga took the infant Prabhasa with her, promising to raise him and return him to Shantanu when he turned sixteen.
For sixteen long years, Shantanu lived in deep depression and lost all interest in his kingdom.
True to her word, Ganga returned sixteen years later and presented the young prince, named Devavrata, to his father.
Devavrata had received the finest education in the universe: archery from the mighty Parashurama and knowledge of the Vedas directly from Brihaspati.
Overjoyed, Shantanu's grief vanished instantly. He welcomed his accomplished son with immense love and crowned him as Yuvraj (Crown Prince).
With Devavrata ably running the administration of the kingdom, King Shantanu lived in peace—until one day, while hunting, he fell in love once more...
